title: 34.3 A 4.75GHz Digital PLL with 45.8fs Integrated-Jitter and 257dB FoM Based on a Voltage-Biased Harmonic-Shaping DCO with Adaptive Common-Mode Resonance Tuning
problem: Digital PLLs for low-jitter synthesis must minimize DCO flicker and white noise, but voltage-biased DCOs require complex tuning-bank segmentation and extensive manual common-mode (CM) resonance tuning that is PVT-sensitive.
method: A voltage-biased DCO with harmonic-shaping architecture employs adaptive common-mode resonance tuning based on second-harmonic amplitude, enabling automatic foreground/background tuning across PVT variations. The approach uses wideband CM resonance expansion via transformer to maintain high CM impedance across the full tuning range.

title: COMET: Towards Practical W4A4KV4 LLMs Serving
problem: Prevalent LLM quantization methods (W8A8 or W4-only) do not fully utilize INT4 tensor cores on modern GPUs and cannot reduce the KV cache memory bottleneck, because quantizing activations to 4-bit causes unacceptable accuracy loss with standard methods, leaving W4A4 impractical.
method: COMET introduces a fine-grained mixed-precision quantization algorithm (FMPQ) that compresses most activations to 4-bit while preserving accuracy by identifying and retaining outlier activations at higher precision (e.g., 8-bit) in a mixed-precision format. On the hardware side, COMET develops a highly optimized W4Ax GPU kernel (supporting both W4A4 and W4A8 mixed-precision GEMM) with a novel mixed-precision data layout that co-locates 4-bit and 8-bit activation elements to enable fast dequantization. The kernel uses GPU software pipelining to overlap data loading and conversion with computation, and introduces fine-grained streaming multiprocessor (SM) scheduling to achieve load balance across SMs. COMET integrates this kernel into a full LLM inference framework with efficient KV4 cache management supporting models like LLaMA-3-70B on a single A100-80G.

title: EPICS: Efficient Parallel Pattern Fault Simulation for Sequential Circuits via Strongly Connected Components
problem: Gate-level fault simulation for large sequential circuits is time-consuming; existing parallel-pattern techniques fail for sequential circuits due to timing dependencies within feedback loops (strongly connected components).
method: EPICS combines loop fusion (compiling simple loops into larger nodes) with event-driven simulation; selects loop entrance nodes via indegree analysis for larger SCCs; implements lazy propagation for internal nodes; strategically mixes compiled and event-driven modes.

title: Enhancing Large-Scale AI Training Efficiency: The C4 Solution for Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Communication Optimization
problem: Large-scale distributed LLM training across thousands of GPUs suffers from efficiency loss due to (1) hardware failures that are slow to detect and isolate, and (2) network traffic collisions that cause prolonged GPU idle time during collective communication synchronization steps.
method: C4 exploits two properties of distributed training workloads: (1) homogeneous, iteration-structured load means hardware anomalies produce detectable syndromes in collective communication patterns, enabling rapid faulty-component identification, isolation, and task restart without waiting for software-level timeouts; (2) collective communication involves a small number of long-lived, predictable flows, allowing C4 to perform proactive traffic planning that eliminates bandwidth contention among these flows and reduces collision-induced queuing.

title: Identifying System-on-Chip Security Assets with Structure-Based Analysis
problem: SoC designs integrate components from multiple sources, creating complex attack surfaces; identifying and protecting security assets (cryptographic keys, sensitive data, control logic) is critical but currently manual and time-intensive, slowing security validation and risk assessment.
method: Automated framework for SoC security asset identification: transforms RTL code into graph representations, applies deep neural networks (DNNs) to classify nodes as security or non-security assets based on structural patterns learned from training data. Graph representation captures connectivity and data flow information.

title: A Full-system, Programmable, and Extensible In-Memory Computing Simulation Framework for Deep Learning
problem: Designing scalable, programmable IMC platforms for modern generative AI (LLMs, DiTs) lacks simulation infrastructure that accurately models device-level physics while supporting full-stack software integration.
method: IMCsim provides full-system simulation: (1) ISA extensions for tensor operations, (2) mappable to eNVM-, SRAM-, or digital IMC architectures, (3) validated against silicon prototypes (22nm MRAM, 28nm SRAM), (4) enables PPA trade-off exploration across workloads.

title: TidalMesh: Topology-Driven AllReduce Collective Communication for Mesh Topology
problem: Existing AllReduce algorithms are topology-aware adaptations of generic algorithms (ring, tree) to physical 2D mesh networks, resulting in a mismatch between logical and physical communication patterns that wastes bandwidth and increases latency.
method: TidalMesh is a topology-driven AllReduce algorithm designed natively for 2D mesh networks. It pushes data flows between endpoint nodes in a wave-like (tidal) pattern that aligns with the mesh grid structure, fully utilizing bidirectional links and minimizing congestion. Sparse TidalMesh minimizes the bandwidth overhead of the base algorithm. Collective communication unrolling enables software pipelining by superimposing different AllReduce phases (ReduceScatter, AllGather) so that compute and communication overlap across multiple concurrent AllReduce operations, effectively hiding collective communication latency.

title: KLIMA: Low-latency mixed-signal In-Memory Computing accelerator for solving arbitrary-order Boolean Satisfiability
problem: Boolean Satisfiability (SAT) solving requires exploring vast search spaces, with conventional CPU/GPU approaches suffering from memory bandwidth and latency bottlenecks. KLIMA addresses solving arbitrary-order SAT problems with single-digit nanosecond latency.
method: KLIMA uses mixed-signal in-memory computing (analog logic with digital interfacing) to perform SAT clause evaluation in memory, eliminating von Neumann bottlenecks by computing directly on stored data using current-mode analog circuits that evaluate Boolean expressions faster than digital logic can fetch operands.

title: EOD: Enabling Low Latency GNN Inference via Near-Memory Concatenate Aggregation
problem: Real-time GNN inference for online services requires an inductive setup where the system must first prepare the computational graph and node features before executing inference, with this preparation step dominating end-to-end latency. The neighborhood explosion problem causes exponential growth in memory access and computation as the number of GNN layers increases.
method: EOD co-designs algorithm and hardware to tackle both challenges. On the algorithmic side, it introduces a precomputation method for training nodes that converts exponential neighborhood aggregation to linear complexity, and a concatenated Zero-Value Compression (ZVC) scheme to compact the stored precomputed hidden features. On the hardware side, EOD implements a Near-Memory Processing (NMP) architecture that performs aggregation directly on ZVC-compressed, concatenated feature data without decompressing to host memory, exploiting the high internal memory bandwidth to eliminate the PCIe/host-memory bottleneck during the preparation stage.

title: Prosperity: Accelerating Spiking Neural Networks via Product Sparsity
problem: Existing SNN accelerators exploit bit sparsity (zero-valued spikes) to skip zero multiplications, but this approach leaves substantial redundancy unexploited: non-zero spike patterns that produce structurally identical inner products across matrix rows are recomputed independently, wasting significant compute.
method: Product Sparsity is a new sparsity paradigm that identifies combinatorially similar binary spike patterns across matrix rows: if two rows share identical non-zero positions, their dot products with the same weight vector are identical and only one needs to be computed, with the result reused for the other. Prosperity implements this via a real-time pattern matching engine that groups rows by their spike pattern hash, computes the inner product once per unique pattern, and distributes results to all matching rows. This is applied to both fully-connected and convolutional layers of SNNs with binary activations.

title: Caracal: A GPU-Resident Sparse LU Solver with Lightweight Fine-Grained Scheduling
problem: Inefficiencies in task scheduling, memory management, and scalability in GPU-resident sparse LU factorization limit the performance of sparse solvers on GPU clusters.
method: Two-level scheduling approach: (1) coarse-grained blocks with sequential scheduling, (2) fine-grained blocks managed with lightweight static scheduler enabling multi-stream parallelism. Intelligent memory caching retains frequently accessed data. 1D block-cyclic matrix distribution optimizes NVLink inter-GPU communication.

title: Modular Architecture for High-Performance and Low Overhead Data Transfers
problem: Traditional file transfer tools suffer from resource underutilization and instability due to fixed configurations or monolithic optimization methods; adapting to changing network/system conditions is difficult.
method: AutoMDT: modular data transfer architecture using deep reinforcement learning (PPO agent) to optimize concurrency levels for read, network, and write operations. Lightweight simulator enables offline training (~45 min) without impacting production networks.

title: 37.8 A 13.5µW 35-Keyword End-to-End Keyword Spotting System Featuring Personalized On-Chip Training in 28nm CMOS
problem: Existing keyword spotting systems recognize only up to 10 keywords with low accuracy for accented speakers, and lack user-specific trainability, limiting personalization for diverse speech patterns and larger vocabularies.
method: The system employs a compact CNN with on-chip training capability, featuring a sine-based convolution with approximate logarithm function as a low-complexity feature extractor. Training occurs on-chip to adapt to individual users, enabling personalization without external servers while maintaining power efficiency through compact architecture and quantized operations.

title: 2D Thermal Contour Modeling of 14 nm SOI FinFET Using Machine Learning for Efficient Thermal Profile Prediction
problem: SOI FinFETs suffer from severe self-heating due to reduced thermal conductivity of silicon-on-insulator substrate. Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations for thermal analysis are time-intensive, limiting rapid device design iteration.
method: ML-based approach combining FEM simulation and machine learning (FSML: FEM-supplemented ML). CNN and VAE models trained on thermal FEM datasets. Datasets generated from Synopsys TCAD FEM simulator for 14 nm SOI FinFET. Evaluation metrics: MSE, accuracy, loss, IoU (Intersection Over Union), SSIM (Structural Similarity).

title: MPI Collectives with Programmable Smart Switches
problem: MPI collective operations are critical for HPC and ML training but incur significant latency and bandwidth overhead. Smart network switches could offload these operations to the network hardware, but integration is lacking.
method: mpitofino: Prototype for offloading MPI collectives onto programmable Ethernet switches (Intel Tofino ASIC). Uses P4 programming language for chip-level processing. Leverages RoCEv2 and RDMA hardware support on NICs. Integrated as a collective provider in Open MPI.

title: Comprehensive Placement and Routing Framework with Guaranteed In-Cell Routability for Synthesizing Complementary-FET Cells
problem: CFET cell layout synthesis faces extreme routing resource scarcity due to vertical transistor stacking; existing generators struggle with in-cell routability and produce suboptimal or infeasible layouts.
method: Three-stage approach: (1) partitioning + quality maintenance for scalability, (2) SMT-based placement with partial routing integration to determine pin positions and ensure routability, (3) progressive metal routing using manual-inspired M0 + ILP-based M1/M2 layers to handle unidirectional constraints.
